main_text.l: libus ex professo agitur, judices non tantum non di-
cuntur Otiosi, sed ab iisdem etiam distinguuntur, uti
ex Cod. Sanhedrin liquet, loco alibi à nobis citato.
X V. Sed si quid denique illud de Otiosis veri
habeat, istud summum inde recte colligi poterit & con-
cludi; usum vocis במלינים vel Otiosorum, tandem se-
quioribus seculis à Judæis Babyloniis ita ampliatum
esse, ut ea præter Veterum morem etiam Doctores
Academicos, eosdemque Iudices, fuerit complexa; haud
secus ac חזן & שליח הציבור qui olim distincti fue-
runt, à recentioribus plerisque ita confunduntur, ut
hactenus Viri in his literis Principes illos putaverint
eosdem. Id autem quicquid sit, nobis certe obesse non
potest; nisi quis ita secum statuat, animumque credere
ex hodiernorum quorundam sive errore, sive abusu vocis,

page.notes: Hebrew words in the line "usum vocis" and "qui olim distincti" are printed in Hebrew letters; the Hebrew for "במלינים" and "חזן ושליח הציבור" are copied as best legible and may be imperfect. The Hebrew "שליח הציבור" is set in a line with the words "& חזן". The "CA" signature is printed at the right; the scan shows the letters faintly. Greek and Hebrew transcriptions are uncertain where marked by the scan quality.
